svg.title: The Soviet Invasion of Afghanistan (December 1979) and The Carter Doctrine (January 1980)
svg.desc: Pearson Edexcel GCSE History regional geopolitical map showing Soviet airborne and armoured invasion routes from the Turkmen, Uzbek, and Tajik SSRs into Herat, Kandahar, Bagram, and Kabul in December 1979, Mujahideen Hindu Kush mountain resistance zones, CIA Operation Cyclone and Pakistani supply routes via Peshawar and Quetta, Revolutionary Iran (1979), and the Persian Gulf / Strait of Hormuz oil lifeline protected by the Carter Doctrine.

g.text: Turkmen · Uzbek · Tajik SSRs (30m Soviet Muslims)
US funds, arms & later Stinger missiles
Arabian Sea · World Oil Tanker Lifeline
USA pledged military force + Rapid Deployment Force to
stop Soviet expansion toward Persian Gulf oil supplies.
Islamic Mujahideen civil war; Amin killed
• Brezhnev Doctrine invoked to stop Islamism
spreading north into Central Asian SSRs.
Carter Doctrine Shield & Oil Tanker Lane
EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY · OPTION P4: END OF DÉTENTE & SECOND COLD WAR
The Soviet Invasion of Afghanistan & The Carter Doctrine
EDEXCEL EXAM TAKEAWAY · CONSEQUENCES OF THE DECEMBER 1979 INVASION
Afghanistan killed Détente overnight: Carter withdrew SALT 2, imposed grain & tech embargoes, proclaimed the
Carter Doctrine, led the 60+ nation 1980 Moscow Olympic boycott, and trapped the USSR in an $8bn/yr "Vietnam".
